{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]] | [[Cookbook:Meat_Recipes|Meat recipes]]

This is a traditional recipe for '''Liverpool scouse''', also known as "lobscouse". The sauce is not thickened, and it is usual to serve with preserved beetroot or red cabbage and white bread with butter. An even more impoverished variety of this dish is 'blind Scouse', which features no meat.

==Ingredients==

* A cheap cut of [[Cookbook:Lamb|lamb]] or mutton (such as breast or forequarter)
* A little [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Onion|Onions]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* [[Cookbook:Carrot|Carrots]], chopped
* Water or meat [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]]
* [[Cookbook:Potato|Potatoes]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]

==Procedure==

# Remove the meat from the bone (if needed), and dice it.
# Heat a little oil in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Add the meat, and [[Cookbook:Browning|brown]] it.
# Add the chopped onions, carrots, and water or meat stock, and as many potatoes as possible.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] until everything is cooked.
